thread:
margo: Heads-up — Pager saw 3x burn in us-west GPU SLI this morning, digging into dashboards now. :mag:
liam: I saw the alert too. Is this the new canary rollout or a traffic spike? any region-specific notes?
margo: Traffic looks normal. Grafana shows queue-length spike on nodepool-gpu-p4 in us-west-2. Im worried it's saturation, not latency noise.
noah: Quick check: prometheus rule `gpu_queue_length_sum / gpu_pool_capacity` spiked to ~0.83 for ~12m. That exceeds our current saturation SLI of 0.7.
esther: Do we have a canonical PromQL for the saturation SLI? People keep reimplementing slightly different variants.
margo: Proposed SLI (draft): fraction of 5m windows in last 30d where per-pool active_queue_ratio < 0.7.
liam: Can you paste the PromQL? Ill add it to the SLO repo.
margo: Sure — here's what I used locally:
```
# per-pool active queue ratio (approx)
sum by(pool) (rate(gpu_active_queue_length[5m]))
/
sum by(pool) (gpu_pool_capacity)
```
Then a rolling window SLI:
```
avg_over_time((sum by(pool)(rate(gpu_active_queue_length[5m])) / sum by(pool)(gpu_pool_capacity) < 0.7)[30d:5m])
```
noah: Two comments: 1) we should use `max_over_time` for short bursts vs sustained, 2) pools have differing capacity (p4 vs a100) so weight by capacity when computing global SLI.
margo: Good call. Id prefer a capacity-weighted aggregate so big pools influence the global SLI proportionally.
liam: For weighting we can use `sum by(pool)(gpu_pool_capacity * (ratio < 0.7)) / sum(gpu_pool_capacity)` — readable and deterministic.
esther: Also want to call out KV-cache eviction correlation — when queue ratio >0.8 we saw a KV cache miss spike TTL-wise. Might be exacerbating tail latency.
noah: For error budget burn reports, Id like a burn rate rule that triggers if 1h burn > 3x expected burn. We have to avoid noisy alerts for short-lived infra blips.
margo: Proposed burn-rate calc: `increase(error_budget_consumed_total[1h]) / (error_budget_total / 30d_in_seconds)` then compare to threshold.
liam: For practical alerting in Alertmanager, recommend two thresholds: warning at 2.0x sustained for 30m, critical at 3.5x sustained for 15m. Keeps ops noise down.
esther: Agree. Also add a suppression for deploy-tagged traffic: if rollout=canary and deployment_age < 1h then mute burn alerts for that pool (we want signal but not immediate page).
noah: Regarding dashboards: we should add a panel that shows capacity-weighted saturation and a stacked view by pool type (p4,a100) plus an annotations row for deploys.
margo: I created a draft Grafana panel and linked it in #eng-sre-dashboards: https://grafana.example.org/d/6gGhS9G/pool-saturation — comments welcomed.
liam: Looks good. Two UX asks: 1) add a single stat with capacity-weighted SLI and SLA target lines, 2) a small table with top 5 pools by contribution to burn.
esther: I'll update the dashboard and add the PromQL into `infra/slo/rules.yaml` as a recording rule so dashboards can use `slo:gpu_saturation_ratio:ratio`.
noah: For rollups across regions, prefer storing per-region recording rules and a final `global_slo` that weights by `region_capacity`. Avoid cross-region queries at dashboard time.
margo: Ops playbook note: if saturation > 0.8 for >20m, action is "drain low-priority workloads from affected pool, spin up burst nodes in neighboring region if autoscale fails" — add to runbook.
liam: Who can own the runbook entry? I can take the burst/autoscale section; esther can own dashboard and recording rule updates.
esther: Ack. Ill PR dashboard + rules. Will include test queries and a small fuzz test to simulate partial pool failures.
sre-bot: Alert muted for pool=p4-us-west if deployment_tag=canary and deployment_age_seconds < 3600 (suppression rule applied).
margo: Thanks all — let's reconvene after rules PR merges. Keeping open to tune thresholds based on 2w of telemetry. :thumbsup:
